exposure: Gestational age at presentation with meconium-stained amniotic fluid (MSAF) (early-term: 37-39 weeks vs. late-term: 40-42 weeks)
outcome: Length of second stage of labor
cohort: The study compared 239 women with early-term pregnancies (37-39 weeks of gestation) presenting with meconium-stained amniotic fluid (MSAF) to 362 women with late-term pregnancies (40-42 weeks of gestation) presenting with MSAF.
finding: In term pregnancies complicated by MSAF, adverse neonatal and maternal delivery outcomes are equivalent regardless of gestational age, although early-term pregnancies had a higher prevalence of gestational diabetes, a shorter second stage of labor, and a longer hospital stay.
